title: Social Sim Arena question bundle v1
description: One week's questions, published together and due together. A bundle IS a batch: `deadline` is the batch deadline from ssa/batches.py (Monday 12:00Z), and it is the only moment a participant has to track. Each question still carries its own `lock_at` -- the arena's clock, 0 to 7 days after the deadline -- and the difference is reported as `horizon_days` so a participant can see which questions ask further ahead. A round's `lock_at` is never the participant's deadline.

timestamp.description: UTC, second precision, trailing Z. The arena publishes no local times: a deadline written in someone's timezone is a deadline someone else reads wrong.

round_id.description: The round this question answers. An answer names it; the arena files the answer at forecasts/<round_id>/<entrant_id>.json.

tracker.description: Which opinion tracker publishes the number, e.g. civiqs or umich_sentiment.

series.description: The specific series inside that tracker. For a profile round this is the representative cell; the full roster is in `cells`.

question.description: The published wording, verbatim. This is what the round is scored against, so it is carried rather than summarised.

unit.description: The unit every number in the answer is in. An answer in the wrong unit scores as a wrong answer, which is why the unit travels with the question rather than being looked up.

target_type.description: Which of the three answer shapes this question takes. It is fixed by the round, not chosen by the entrant: a single number is not a weak answer to a profile question, it is an answer to a different question.

release_at.description: When the real number is scheduled to be published.

lock_at.description: The arena's internal freeze, release - 48h. Informational for a participant: what an answer is due by is the bundle's `deadline`, which is earlier.

horizon_days.description: deadline -> lock, in days. It varies across a bundle and it varies identically for every entrant, which is what makes it a property of the question worth reporting rather than a head start worth removing.

resolve.description: The resolution rule, verbatim from the round definition: which source, which value, which adjustment.

cells.description: profile_energy only: every cell the answer must carry. All of them or none -- the energy score is a norm over the whole vector, so a profile with a hole has no score.

items.description: ranking_list only, and only for a fixed-basket round: the exact items to permute. Absent means the round is a free choice from a named universe, and `ranking_length` then says how many to name.

ranking_length.description: ranking_list only: how many items the answer lists. Carried separately from `items` because a free-choice ranking round (the Wikipedia top-10) has a length but no basket, and a length inferred from prose in `unit` is a length nobody can validate against.

exclusions.description: ranking_list only, free-choice rounds: the id of the rule saying which titles cannot appear. Carried because the rule is part of the question -- a title it drops cannot be part of any answer -- and an entrant who never sees it finds out at scoring time.

batch_id.description: ssa.batches.batch_of(lock_at), e.g. batch-2026-09-14. A response bundle repeats it, so a payload cannot be filed against a week it was not written for.

deadline.description: The one moment every answer in this bundle is due by. Filing early is allowed and costs nothing: the deadline is shared, and the baselines the scores divide by freeze at this same instant, so nobody is compared against a reference that read news they could not.

published_at.description: deadline - 7d. When the bundle became available, so a participant has a full week.

questions.description: Every round governed by this deadline, in lock order. A bundle mixes scalar, profile and ranking rounds; nothing about answering one shape depends on the others.
